How to write a job ad with AI: one-line prompt vs a proper brief

Prompt A was "Write a job ad for a barista." It came back with "passionate", "fast-paced" and no hours or pay.

Prompt B was a short brief. Copy this:

"Write a job ad for [ROLE] at [BUSINESS] in [AREA]. Hours: [DAYS + TIMES]. Pay: [RATE]. Must have: [2–3 MUST-HAVES]. Nice to have: [ANY]. Why work here: [2–3 REAL REASONS]. How to apply: [STEPS]. Tone: friendly and plain, like we talk. Under 120 words. Don't use 'fast-paced' or 'rockstar'."

On an invented café, B put the hours and pay in the second line, kept the real perks and ended with a clear next step: 3 lines about you, then a short paid trial shift.

The AI can only be specific if you are. Two minutes on the brief does the work.
